stories.headline: Sources: 49ers Pro Bowl FB Juszczyk (knee) expected out 2-3 weeks
stories.summary: 49ers Pro Bowl fullback Kyle Juszczyk suffered a knee sprain and bone bruise that is expected to sideline him for two to three weeks, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
stories.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- San Francisco 49ers Pro Bowl fullback Kyle Juszczyk suffered a knee sprain and bone bruise that is expected to sideline him for two to three weeks, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Juszczyk sustained the injury during San Francisco's 24-14 victory over the Denver Broncos on Sunday. An MRI performed Monday confirmed the nature of his injury.

With 14:03 to go, Niners quarterback Brock Purdy scrambled to his left and found Juszczyk open down the sideline for a 16-yard gain. Broncos defensive back Jahdae Barron delivered a big hit to Juszczyk's knee and midsection, and Juszczyk stayed down for a few minutes as the Niners medical team rushed to help.

Niners personnel helped Juszczyk to the sideline, where he entered the medical tent and stayed for a bit before watching the rest of the game on the bench. The 49ers quickly ruled out a potential return for Juszczyk, who finished with two catches for 28 yards.

Juszczyk, who has been selected to the past 10 Pro Bowls, has four receptions for 55 yards and a touchdown this season.

Safety Marques Sigle (ankle) and slot cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder) also suffered injures Sunday that did not allow them to finish the game.

Sigle suffered a pair of injuries Sunday, initially departing early in the third quarter with a stinger. He returned on Denver's next possession but was injured with 2:15 left when he hurt his ankle near Denver's sideline. He did not return after making six tackles on the day.

Stout hurt his shoulder in the third quarter and jogged to the locker room to be evaluated soon after Juszczyk's injury early in the fourth. Stout returned with 2:07 to go but then left again and did not play during the Broncos' final few snaps. He also finished with six tackles.

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey weekly picks: Can't get MacKinnon? Add his linemate instead!
stories.summary: Begin your fantasy hockey week with forwards, defensemen, goalies and streamers to add to your lineup.
stories.body:
The puck has dropped, the overreactions are flowing and the waiver wire is already moving. Welcome back to the fantasy hockey grind. A handful of games is nowhere near enough to rewrite anyone's draft board, but it is enough to spot new roles, new linemates and new power-play deployments before your leaguemates catch on.

The second full scoring period runs from Oct. 5 to Oct. 11, with 47 games on the slate. The Carolina Hurricanes, Ottawa Senators, Philadelphia Flyers and Pittsburgh Penguins have the advantage for head-to-head leagues with four games apiece, while the Columbus Blue Jackets, Calgary Flames, Edmonton Oilers, Florida Panthers, Los Angeles Kings and New Jersey Devils are stuck at two.

Daily lineup managers, take note: Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Sunday are the light nights, with four or fewer games each. The Capitals hit the sweet spot for streaming if your league caps weekly transactions, averaging only 5.67 other teams in action on their three game nights, and the Jets (6.33) are close behind. Most puck drops are 7 p.m. ET or later, but set an alarm for a 1 p.m. start on Saturday and 5 p.m. on Sunday.

Every Monday, we'll mine the waiver wire for lesser-rostered performers who have the potential to help fantasy teams in a variety of leagues. We'll also present several strong streaming candidates for the immediate week ahead.

See more: Rankings | Projections | Mock Draft Lobby

Draft guide | Cheat sheet | October preview | Sign up

Forwards

Vasily Podkolzin, LW/RW, Edmonton Oilers (4.03 FPPG, 34.7% available): With Zach Hyman sidelined, Podkolzin has inherited the best seat in the house: the top line with Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl, plus two-thirds of the Oilers' top power-play time. The trio is 4-0 on goals at 5-on-5 through 26 minutes together, and Podkolzin already has three power-play points. It's only a two-game week, so add him for the role rather than the schedule, and expect him to slide back toward last season's 1.48 FPPG once Hyman returns, but consider a longer trial in leagues that count hits.

Artturi Lehkonen, LW, Colorado Avalanche (5.40 FPPG, 45.8% available): Any winger riding shotgun with Nathan MacKinnon and Martin Necas deserves a look, and Lehkonen has spent nearly three-quarters of his even-strength time there through two games. Temper the excitement over three goals and an assist, though: the trio is 3-0 on goals at 5-on-5 while generating just 40% of the shot attempts, and Lehkonen is on the second power-play unit. He has a higher ceiling than last season's 1.52 FPPG for as long as the top-line role holds. A road trip through Winnipeg and Calgary helps, with the Avalanche's three opponents combining for the ninth-friendliest slate for top-six forwards.

Cole Perfetti, LW, Winnipeg Jets (4.45 FPPG, 81.3% available): All four of Perfetti's points have come on the power play, where the Jets' top unit is generating a blistering 7.52 shot attempts per two minutes with him on the ice. At even strength, he's skating 84 percent of his minutes with Mark Scheifele and Kyle Connor, and while that line is 0-2 on goals, it ranks 26th of 133 lines (minimum five minutes per game) in shot attempts rate. Bonus for daily leagues: all three Jets games land on light nights.

Jordan Eberle, RW, Seattle Kraken (2.83 FPPG, 68.8% available): Eberle has opened the season on the Kraken top line with Chandler Stephenson and Bobby McMann, and the trio is 3-0 on goals at 5-on-5 with a healthy 54.2% share of the shot attempts. He's also seeing half of Seattle's power-play time on the second unit, which accounts for two of his three points. Two of the three Kraken games fall on light nights, making him a sneaky daily-league option.

Jimmy Snuggerud, RW, St. Louis Blues (2.15 FPPG, 65.4% available): Snuggerud is back where he finished last season, on the top line with Robert Thomas and Dylan Holloway, and he's added a spot on the top power-play unit. That unit has been sputtering (1.76 shot attempts per two minutes), but the week offers relief: the Blackhawks, Sharks and Blue Jackets combine for the eighth-friendliest slate for top-six forwards, and two of the three games come against bottom-10 penalty kills.

See also:

Quinton Byfield, C, Los Angeles Kings (2.60 FPPG, 34.1% available)

Eeli Tolvanen, LW/RW, New York Rangers (2.33 FPPG, 56.4% available)

Bobby McMann, LW/RW, Seattle Kraken (2.80 FPPG, 59.0% available)

Viktor Arvidsson, RW, Detroit Red Wings (2.25 FPPG, 89.8% available)

Mikael Granlund, C/LW, Anaheim Ducks (2.10 FPPG, 39.3% available)

Igor Chernyshov, LW, San Jose Sharks (2.90 FPPG, 93.4% available)

Defense

Mattias Samuelsson, D, Buffalo Sabres (2.20 FPPG, 36.0% available): A 2.01 FPPG performer across 78 games last season, Samuelsson is still available in more than a third of leagues despite opening the season on the Sabres top pair with Rasmus Dahlin. He doesn't touch the power play, so the value comes from 21-plus minutes a night and everything that comes with them. The pair is controlling 69.4 percent of the shot attempts at 5-on-5, and all three of the Sabres games this week are at home.

Brayden McNabb, D, Vegas Golden Knights (2.33 FPPG, 89.2% available): McNabb and Shea Theodore have been on the ice for six goals for and only two against at 5-on-5 through 43 minutes together, and McNabb has four assists to show for it. That pace won't last for a defender without power-play time, but the hits and blocks (2.8 of his 7.0 fantasy points) give him a reliable floor in deeper formats.

Vladislav Gavrikov, D, New York Rangers (2.58 FPPG, 54.5% available): Thirteen blocked shots through four games is the headline for Gavrikov, accounting for the bulk of his 10.3 fantasy points. Playing more than 21 minutes a night next to Adam Fox gives him enough offensive spillover to make the floor worth chasing, with two points in his past three games. Two of the Rangers' three games fall on light nights.

See also:

Jared Spurgeon, D, Minnesota Wild (2.90 FPPG, 95.7% available)

Luca Cagnoni, D, San Jose Sharks (3.35 FPPG, 68.1% available)

Adam Larsson, D, Seattle Kraken (2.07 FPPG, 59.8% available)

Martin Fehervary, D, Washington Capitals (1.95 FPPG, 67.7% available)

Goaltenders

Jesper Wallstedt, G, Minnesota Wild (6.54 FPP60, 19.7% available): The timeshare will have to wait. Filip Gustavsson landed on IR with a hip injury and isn't expected back until at least Nov. 1, which hands Wallstedt the Wild crease for the rest of October. He's made the most of it so far, with two wins and a .957 save percentage. The road trip through Buffalo, Tampa Bay and Florida is one of the week's tougher goalie schedules, but a month of near-full workload makes him a must-add in the one in five leagues where he's still sitting there.

Joel Hofer, G, St. Louis Blues (12.00 FPP60, 20.7% available): Hofer and Jordan Binnington split the first two Blues starts, and Hofer's perfect outing earned him 12.0 fantasy points. One game is a tiny sample, so lean on the schedule instead: no back-to-back sets and two top-10 goalie matchups against the Blackhawks and Blue Jackets. Even a split of the three games should land him a good one.

Mackenzie Blackwood, G, Colorado Avalanche (4.20 FPP60, 15.9% available): Enjoy it while it lasts. This is likely the last week goalies like Blackwood are this easy to find on the wire, before the rest of your league wakes up from its draft-day hangover. The Avalanche have the best goalie schedule of the week, and Blackwood has started and won both games so far. The catch is the back-to-back set on Wednesday and Thursday. The Flames on Thursday are the No. 1 matchup for fantasy goalies, so here's hoping he draws that half.

See also:

Joey Daccord, G, Seattle Kraken (7.63 FPP60, 59.5% available)

Lukas Dostal, G, Anaheim Ducks (4.46 FPP60, 66.4% available)

Jet Greaves, G, Columbus Blue Jackets (0.00 FPP60, 38.3% available)

Short-term streamers

Shane Pinto, C/RW, Ottawa Senators (1.80 FPPG, 85.5% available): The Senators have played only once, so Pinto's numbers don't tell us much yet. What does matter is a four-game week whose opponents combine for the second-friendliest slate for top-six forwards. Pinto's third line with Claude Giroux and Michael Amadio still logged more than 20 minutes in the opener, and he adds second-unit power-play time. That's plenty of opportunity for a streamer.

Tommy Novak, C/LW, Pittsburgh Penguins (4.15 FPPG, 91.6% available): Novak is skating with Evgeni Malkin at even strength and on the Penguins top power-play unit, a combination that has produced four points in two games. Pittsburgh's four games, three of them on light nights, make him a natural fit for daily leagues. Just know the 5-on-5 numbers (43.2% of the shot attempts) are less rosy than the scoring.

Kris Letang, D, Pittsburgh Penguins (2.45 FPPG, 38.4% available): Letang is off to a three-assist start through two games, and the Penguins schedule does the rest: four games, three on light nights, against opponents who combine for the second-friendliest slate for top-four defenders. He's only on the second power-play unit, so treat this as a one-week rental.

Jackson Blake, RW, Carolina Hurricanes (1.73 FPPG, 54.2% available): No team has a better schedule for forwards this week. The Hurricanes play four times, and their opponents combine to allow more fantasy points to top-six forwards than any other team's slate, with two of the games against bottom-10 penalty kills. Blake is still on his dominant playoff line with Taylor Hall and Logan Stankoven, and is averaging more than seven minutes a night on the power play, where both of his points have come.

William Eklund, LW, Ottawa Senators (0.50 FPPG, 44.0% available): Like Pinto, Eklund is a bet on the Senators schedule rather than his quiet lone game. His spot on the top power-play unit gets two cracks at bottom-10 penalty kills in a four-game week.

Arturs Silovs, G, Pittsburgh Penguins (4.34 FPP60, 76.4% available): Silovs has started and won both Penguins games despite a shaky .886 save percentage. With four games, including a back-to-back set on Friday and Saturday, he should see at least two starts, and the Jets and Blue Jackets are both top-10 matchups for fantasy goalies. Steer clear of the Saturday date with the Stars, who rank last for fantasy points allowed to goalies.

stories.headline: Knicks' Karl-Anthony Towns not expecting contract extension soon
stories.summary: Karl-Anthony Towns says the chances "don't look good" for him getting a new extension with the Knicks before the start of the regular season.
stories.body:
The New York Knicks take the court for their first preseason game Monday night, but one of the key players in last season's championship run remains at odds with the team over a contract extension.

"It don't look good," Karl-Anthony Towns said Monday of getting a new contract in place before the start of the regular season.

Towns is eligible for a four-year deal worth over $276 million. He is due $57 million this season and has a $61.1 million player option for next season.

Sources told ESPN's Shams Charania that the Knicks' latest offer to Towns was a four-year deal worth approximately $200 million.

A six-time All-Star, Towns was a catalyst for the Knicks' playoff run last season, averaging 15.9 points, 10.6 rebounds and 4.9 assists as New York won the title in a five-game Finals over the San Antonio Spurs.

Does that mean the Knicks should reward Towns for his hand in ending a 53-year title drought?

"No s---, Sherlock," Towns said. "I just won a championship. You'd think it was pretty easy. Unless you guys [reporters] think I have something else to prove."

Knicks owner James Dolan has said the team will not go into the second spending apron, which means tough decisions will need to be made. New York did not re-sign backup center Mitchell Robinson this offseason. Robinson, who was the longest-tenured Knick on last year's team, signed with the Boston Celtics.

Towns said that he's aware of the challenges of maintaining a championship core but that in his estimation the team has not done enough to compromise.

"Simply put, I want to do something that can keep the team together and work with the Knicks and also values me," Towns said. "None of those things have come close to happening."

Information from ESPN's Vincent Goodwill was used in this report.

stories.headline: JJ Gabriel representatives demanded game time at Manchester United - sources
stories.summary: Representatives of JJ Gabriel demanded that the teenager played at least 20 minutes in games against Sabah FK, Brighton and Bournemouth before beginning talks about signing a scholarship with Manchester United, sources have told ESPN.
stories.body:
Representatives of JJ Gabriel demanded that the teenager played at least 20 minutes in games against Sabah FK, Brighton and Bournemouth before beginning talks about signing a scholarship with Manchester United, sources have told ESPN.

Gabriel, 15, has not trained with United since walking out on the club ahead of their Carabao Cup tie with Brighton on Sept. 16.

He is pictured in United's squad photo, which was released on Monday. However, the image was taken nearly a month ago and sources have told ESPN there is little sign of a reconciliation with the club.

Gabriel's representatives believe certain promises made by Man United have also been broken, sources told ESPN.

Gabriel's representatives have been approached by ESPN for comment.

Gabriel, who turns 16 on Tuesday, was due to make his first team debut against Brighton before representatives demanded United cancel his registration over a row about his playing time.

He made his first-team debut in a preseason friendly against Atlético Madrid in the summer, but was omitted from the squad for the Champions League.

Sources have told ESPN that representatives told United he must play at least 20 minutes against Sabah, Brighton and in the Premier League fixture against Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Oct. 25 before entering discussions over a scholarship.

Gabriel could have signed a pre-agreement from his 16th birthday on Oct. 6.

With it looking increasingly likely that Gabriel will leave, United, according to sources, are prepared to take legal action if there is evidence of other clubs approaching Gabriel outside of the rules.

They have yet to receive a formal enquiry.

A number of clubs have been linked with a move including Barcelona and Real Madrid.

Despite a breakdown in relations with Gabriel's camp, sources have told ESPN that they continue to believe Old Trafford is the best place for him to develop.

Club officials have made a number of attempts to check on his well-being since he stopped reporting for training.

- Barcelona sporting director: No interest in Man United's JJ Gabriel

- Rooney: 'Disappointing' if 'top player' JJ Gabriel leaves Man United

- Why Man United's wantaway wonderkid, JJ Gabriel, is so highly rated

Sources insist they have made every effort to show he has a pathway to the first team, including assigning coaches and specialist staff -- who usually only work with senior players -- to ensure he's prepared for the demands of professional football.

United also accepted a demand from Gabriel to be given the No.77 squad number for this season and petitioned the Premier League on his behalf to allow him to have the name "Gabriel JR" on his shirt.

Sources close to United insist they have prioritised Gabriel's well-being throughout his time at Old Trafford.

There has been a feeling internally that his representatives -- including members of his family -- have been more keen for the forward to break records rather than focus on his long-term development.

United, according to sources, chose not to punish Gabriel when he missed a week of preseason training with the academy before his step up to the first-team because of a feeling that he could not have been solely responsible for the decision.

Sources have told ESPN that there's genuine concern at Old Trafford that Gabriel is not having an influence on decisions which are affecting his career.

stories.headline: Singapore Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Formula 1's original night race is back as drivers prepare for the ultimate challenge around the Marina Bay Circuit in Singapore.
stories.body:
Formula 1's original night race is back as drivers prepare for the ultimate challenge around the Marina Bay Circuit in Singapore.

It will also be the sixth and final sprint race of the season as Singapore hosts it for the first time.

Max Verstappen claimed his first victory of the season at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, while Kimi Antonelli extended his lead in the title championship to 84 points from George Russell.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 17th round of the season.

- Bahrain GP was the worst indictment of F1's new engine regs yet

- Could Malaysia return to F1 calendar? The state of play despite Sepang travel chaos

- Max Verstappen wins disrupted Bahrain GP, Kimi Antonelli extends title lead as George Russell retires

Singapore Grand Prix schedule
All times in BST

Friday, October 9

Practice One: 9.30 a.m. - 10.30 a.m.

Sprint Qualifying: 1.30 p.m. - 2.14 p.m.

Saturday, October 10

Sprint: 10 a.m. - 11 a.m.

Qualifying: 2 p.m. - 3 p.m.

Sunday, October 11

Singapore Grand Prix: 1 p.m.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Singapore Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Marina Bay Street Circuit

Singapore is one of the toughest challenges on the calendar for drivers due to the intense humidity and physically demanding nature of the circuit.

But this time round the drivers will have had a chance to get used to the humid conditions after racing in Malaysia for the Bahrain Grand Prix last weekend.

The Marina Bay Circuit has been on the calendar since 2008 and is one of the standout tracks. The race takes place at night with its breathtaking views of the city's skyline as cars make their way through the tight and twisty circuit.

Drivers can lose around 3kg in body weight after each race due to the amount they sweat.

Singapore Grand Prix

Circuit: Marina Bay Street Circuit; Singapore

Previous winners in Singapore

2014: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2015: Sebastian Vettel (Ferrari)

2016: Nico Rosberg (Mercedes)

2017: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2018: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2019: Sebastian Vettel (Ferrari)

2022: Sergio Pérez (Red Bull)

2023: Carlos Sainz (Ferrari)

2024: Lando Norris (McLaren)

2025: George Russell (Mercedes)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 2008

Lap record: 1:33.808 Lewis Hamilton (2025)

Most wins: Sebastian Vettel has the most wins with five (2011-2013, 2015 and 2019). From the current grid, Hamilton has four wins (2009, 2014, 2017-2018) and Fernando Alonso with two (2008 and 2010). Pérez (2022), Sainz (2023), Norris (2024) and Russell (2025) have all won a race each here.

Most poles: Vettel (2011, 2013, 2015, 2017) and Hamilton (2009, 2012, 2014, 2018) share the pole record with four each. From the current grid, Charles Leclerc (2019, 2022) has had two pole positions here.

Weather forecast

The weather for the Singapore Grand Prix is set to be thundery showers and light winds throughout the weekend, with highs of 34°C on Friday. The temperature is forecast to drop a degree for the remainder of the weekend.

What happened last time out?
Russell claimed pole position in Singapore last year and crossed the line 0.182 seconds clear of Red Bull's Verstappen, with McLaren's Oscar Piastri behind.

Russell took his second win of the season, but there was plenty of other drama during the race, especially at McLaren.

Norris, who started in fifth, knocked into Piastri when trying to pass him in the first corner. Piastri managed to gain some ground towards the end of the race, but he had to settle for fourth on the day McLaren lifted the trophy for the constructors' title.

Piastri's drivers' championship lead to Norris was separated by only 22 points with six races left of the season.

Who will win this year?

One to watch this weekend is Red Bull and Verstappen after he won the race last weekend. The team brought major upgrades two races ago and improvements to its overall performance has been evident.

Russell, who suffered a major blow to his championship hopes after retiring last time out, will be looking to maximise the points on offer across the weekend.

Mercedes are expected to be strong, while Ferrari are quick in cornering speed. Hamilton has won four times here, so could be a threat. McLaren's Norris and Piastri fell under the radar and struggled for pace in Malaysia.

All will be to play for under the lights in Singapore as we head into the business end of the season.

stories.headline: Every team's odds to win the World Series: Brewers closing in on favorite Dodgers
stories.summary: Every MLB team's odds to win the 2026 World Series as the playoffs continue.
stories.body:
After being the best team in MLB's regular season, the Milwaukee Brewers are inching closer and closer to World Series favorite status, achieving +310 championship odds after their thrilling walk-off win in Game 2 of the National League Divisional Series against the San Diego Padres, who are now the longest team on the odds board at 45-1.

Another thing that helped Milwaukee close the gap was a Game 2 loss by the Los Angeles Dodgers, who lengthened from +160 to +220 after falling to the Atlanta Braves, who improved to +750 after coming into the divisional round at +850 and lengthening somewhat following a Game 1 loss.

The New York Yankees came into the American League Divisional Series tied with the Milwaukee Brewers at +500 for the second-best odds to win the World Series, and as -120 favorites to advance past the Tampa Bay Rays, just the eighth time on record that a 1 seed has been an underdog in an LDS, according to ESPN Research. Tampa Bay immediately flipped the script on New York with a Game 1 win, moving from +800 to +550 for the championship, while the Yankees lengthened to +750.

stories.headline: What's next: Will Silva's first title defense be against Shevchenko?
stories.summary: The most likely opponent and a wild card for the winners and losers on the UFC 332 main card.
stories.body:
The UFC has a new women's flyweight champion for the first time in over two years following the UFC 332 main event in Salt Lake City on Saturday night. And with a new champion comes brand-new matchups. After winning the belt via unanimous decision over Wang Cong, Natalia Silva will have no shortage of challengers looking for their shot at gold.

Also on the UFC 332 fight card, rising men's bantamweight contender Payton Talbott made quick work of former two-time men's flyweight champion Deiveson Figueiredo in the co-main event. Talbott could take on a top-ranked contender in his next Octagon appearance. And a handful of young prospects earned impressive first-round knockout victories.

Here's what's next for the top stars of UFC 332.

Natalia Silva, women's flyweight champion

Who should be next: Valentina Shevchenko

The state of the UFC's women's divisions is not ideal. We haven't seen a bantamweight title fight all year, due to injuries to Kayla Harrison. Mackenzie Dern is the strawweight champion, but (fair or not) there is a pretty significant need for her to fight Zhang Weili to validate her standing as the top 115-pound fighter in the world, since Zhang vacated her belt, never lost it in competition. Now the same is true of the flyweight title. Silva has the longest active win streak at 125 pounds and might be the best in the world, but she'll battle for that perception until she fights Shevchenko. We'll have to see how long Shevchenko is out, but this fight needs to happen as soon as possible.

Wild card: Erin Blanchfield

Blanchfield has looked like future champion material since she debuted with the UFC at 22 years old in 2021. She's now five years into her UFC career, and she is 8-1 with one learning experience in the form of a five-round decision loss to Manon Fiorot in 2024. She's still only 27 and could well prove to be the future of this weight class. She's got a tough matchup scheduled against Jasmine Jasudavicius on Oct. 17. If she gets past that unscathed, the UFC could easily book her with Silva as soon as possible, instead of waiting for Shevchenko.

Payton Talbott, men's bantamweight
Who should be next: Sean O'Malley

It has to be done. O'Malley was once the darling of the bantamweight division. Now it's Talbott, and it's hard to deny this matchup. Now, the UFC is almost certainly already looking at O'Malley for an upcoming title fight. Especially if Petr Yan defeats Merab Dvalishvili at UFC 333 later this month, O'Malley is the favorite to face Yan next. But if UFC fans were polled, the more anticipated fight might honestly be O'Malley vs. Talbott. Not to get out of control here, but this could headline a numbered event.

Wild card: Farid Basharat

This would be the anti-O'Malley booking. The UFC doesn't love that Basharat has mostly decisions on his record -- so much so that there's been some uncertainty about his security with the promotion. He's ranked in the top 10 by the UFC but in a spot to defend his spot (not attack). This is the kind of athlete who might need to fight down the rankings. Enter Talbott.

Ateba Gautier, middleweight
Who should be next: Loser of Bo Nickal vs. Joe Pyfer on Dec. 12

Hear me out: Gautier's hype train took a major, major hit with the first-round knockout loss to Roman Kopylov. There's no way around it. He took a step up in competition, and fell very flat. In this situation, the UFC can quietly step him back to the prelims somewhere -- or it can create a story. Gautier's stock took a hit but he is still extremely dangerous. There's still intrigue attached to him. Nickal is coming off a strong win at the White House over Kyle Daukaus, but there are still question marks around him. Pyfer is riding high after a finish of Israel Adesanya in his last bout. Whoever loses between Nickal and Pyfer would still be in position for a compelling bout. What's more compelling than this? There is still a way for the UFC to use what's left of the hype around Gautier and make a fight fans will want to watch.

Wild card: Loser of Daukaus vs. Marc-Andre Barriault on Oct. 17

This would be an appropriate next step that would teach us more about Gautier. Kopylov is a legitimate (for lack of a better word) gatekeeper, and Daukaus and Andre Barriault are also proven veterans. Either would challenge Gautier and offer him a chance at redemption.

stories.headline: Nigerian connection runs through Mystics rise as Kiki Iriafen breaks out in playoff run
stories.summary: Fresh from helping team USA win the World Cup last month, Kiki Iriafen's second WNBA season ended with a first round elimination to the Atlanta Dream.
stories.body:
Fresh from helping USA win the World Cup last month, Kiki Iriafen's second WNBA season ended with a first round elimination to the Atlanta Dream, but finishing the game with yet another double-double was an indication of just how quickly the Nigerian-American forward has grown into a central piece of the Washington Mystics' present.

Iriafen helped herself to 15 points and 16 rebounds in Washington's 93-75 loss to the Atlanta Dream, completing her first postseason with double-doubles in both games of the first-round series for an average of 15 points and 15 rebounds in the playoffs after a regular season in which she emerged as Washington's leading rebounder and one of their top three scorers.

Alongside her for much of that run was Michaela Onyenwere - another Nigerian-American forward whose contribution came from a different place. The 2021 WNBA Rookie of the Year came to Washington with five seasons of league experience to help the youngest roster in the WNBA and became enough of a veteran voice that her teammates began calling her "Coach Mic."

And just like she did on her Draft night when strutting it out in a dress that reflected her Nigerian heritage, Iriafen says she is driven by the Nigerian spirit

"My Nigerian heritage has been something that I've always wanted to promote," she said. "Michaela and I were just talking about what should we do. Like, we should go celebrate. But it's super special. My Nigerian heritage has been something that I've always wanted to promote. I am Nigerian American, but I feel like both sides of me are equally as important to me."

Together, both have given Washington the Nigerian connection within a team that improved from 16 wins in 2025 to a franchise-record 28 this season and returned to the playoffs for the first time since 2023.

Iriafen's rise, to go with the likes of USA teammate Sonia Citron, and Shakira Austin, was at the heart of that improvement.

After averaging 13.3 points and 8.5 rebounds as a rookie, the 23-year-old increased those numbers to 15.3 points and 9.5 rebounds this season while shooting better than 50% from the field. She finished behind Austin and Citron in scoring and led the Mystics in rebounding, narrowly ahead of Austin.

She also recorded a Mystics single-season record 23 double-doubles, and earned a second consecutive All-Star selection - numbers that helped get her onto Team USA's World Cup roster.

The postseason provided another test - one that Iriafen confronted head on, even if it was her first experience.

Foul trouble in Game 1 meant she played only 23 minutes against Atlanta, but still finished with 15 points and 14 rebounds. Nine of those rebounds came on the offensive end, tying a Washington franchise record for offensive rebounds in a game and helping the Mystics outrebound the Dream 50-31.

"I really felt like I wasn't able to help my team in the first half, so I wanted to do that for my teammates," Iriafen said.

Game 2 was much better, as she stayed on the floor for more than 35 minutes. Her 30 rebounds over the two games were the second-most by a player through her first two WNBA playoff games.

The numbers continued a progression that began almost immediately after Washington selected her with the No. 4 pick in the 2025 draft. Initially, the Mystics leaned heavily on Iriafen's rebounding, transition running and ability to finish around the basket. Now, her offensive responsibilities have gradually expanded to include more post touches, screening actions and opportunities to make decisions with the ball.

Her development has also come alongside Citron - Washington's other cornerstone from the 2025 draft. Citron led the Mystics in playoff scoring with 25 points in each game against Atlanta, while Iriafen controlled the glass.

The partnership leaves Washington with two young players who have already translated regular-season production into the postseason - one that coach Sydney Johnson was pleased with as he singled both out for praise.

"I'm sitting beside two players who played their first playoff games, and there was a lot of good stuff out there," he said. "I'm immensely disappointed for the result, but I also think what this group has accomplished and how the DC community has rallied around this group has been amazing. They've written history. I am excited to take this first step forward with Kiki and Sonia and our whole group."

For Iriafen, that development has unfolded alongside an identity she has repeatedly said matters a lot to her.

"Being Nigerian is huge for me," Iriafen told House of Victory earlier this year. "It's my culture, it's a big part of who I am.

"There are so many young Nigerian hoopers and young Nigerians that I'm an inspiration to and I just want to showcase that being Nigerian is cool."

That connection was there well before she played her first WNBA game. Who can forget Kiki owning the show at the 2025 WNBA draft in a custom dress designed by Nigerian designer Nneka Alexander, while accompanied by members of her family equally attired in traditional Nigerian clothing?

"My parents always say Naija no dey carry last," she said. "So I feel like in everything that I do, I try to strive for that. So that's kind of the motto of my life.

"Something in Nigeria is the resources aren't always as equal, but just understanding that it doesn't matter how you get there, there's still an opportunity. There's still a way. So I just really want to carry myself with class and really truly be a great role model."

The draft took her to Washington, which offered an even bigger connection to Nigeria, with its huge Nigerian population.

A year later, the Mystics added Onyenwere, whose route to the capital was considerably longer. Selected sixth overall by New York in 2021, Onyenwere won WNBA Rookie of the Year before stops with Phoenix and Chicago. Washington signed her to a multiyear deal this year and immediately installed her in a starting lineup filled with younger players.

Onyenwere, 26 years old when the season began, was the oldest player on the roster.

"We call her 'Coach Mic.' She knows what she's talking about," Iriafen said. "She's a great leader, great teammate and great person."

The connection between them predates the Mystics. They first crossed paths when Iriafen was a high school prospect considering UCLA and Onyenwere was playing for the Bruins.

Their Nigerian heritage provided another common thread. Onyenwere's father Peter competed for Nigeria in track and field, and her grandmother became one of the memorable images of the 2021 WNBA draft when she danced in traditional Nigerian clothing behind Onyenwere during a television interview when her name was called.

"I am just so proud to be Nigerian, and I never let anyone forget it," Onyenwere said. "I make sure I let people know I am Nigerian because it is a big part of who I am.

"From Draft Night, I was getting messages from young Nigerian kids who are in Nigeria, saying you are an inspiration. You don't really think those things until you see those messages. Like, I am influencing people in a different continent."

Both women have also represented the United States internationally - a clear sign of the dual identity they have carried and basked in through their basketball careers. Iriafen helped the United States win the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup, appearing in four games during the Americans' unbeaten run to the title.

Onyenwere represented USA Basketball in both 3x3 and 5-on-5 competition in 2019. She played on the American 3x3 circuit and later helped the United States win silver at the Pan American Games.

Nigeria did attempt to bring Onyenwere into the D'Tigress program for the 2024 Paris Olympics, but she was unable to join the team after failing to receive clearance in time.

In adding to the Nigerian connection, her role in Washington this season has been more about helping to provide stability around a young core.

Onyenwere averaged 9.0 points during the regular season while starting alongside Iriafen, Austin and Citron. She scored eight points in the opening playoff loss to Atlanta before adding 12 in Game 2.

Washington's season ended there, but Iriafen's first experience of playoff basketball provided another marker in a second season in which her responsibilities and production grew and both playoff games provided a clear measure of how far her role has expanded and where Washington could take it next.

She finished the two-game series averaging 15 points and 15 rebounds, with 13 offensive rebounds, after leading Washington in rebounding during the regular season and establishing career highs in both scoring and rebounding.

"This whole season has just been just a learning process for me," Iriafen said after Game 2. "It was nothing like my first season.

"I feel like just even during my undergrad, doing tough majors and still being a professional athlete, just showcasing that, whatever you put your mind to that you can do it."

For the Mystics, the next part of that learning process will be figuring out how much more Iriafen can handle. They already have one of the league's most productive young rebounders and an increasingly reliable interior scorer. Her three assists in Game 2 also offered a glimpse of how her role could expand as a passer and decision-maker.

Onyenwere, meanwhile, provided an experienced voice alongside her during that development, four years after becoming WNBA Rookie of the Year herself, giving the Mystics a Nigerian-American one-two punch.

The season may have ended earlier than they or the Mystics wanted, but it also provided a silver lining, with Washington back in the playoffs and Iriafen having experienced the stage that she wanted, even if she failed to conquer it. For now.

"Playoffs are the biggest stage," Iriafen said after Game 1. "This is the stage we want to be on."

On the evidence of this run, it is one that she will be returning to for the foreseeable future. And she will continue to be driven by that Naija no dey carry last spirit.

stories.headline: Magpies likely to hold De Goey as Pendlebury departs
stories.summary: The door has been left ajar for Collingwood to trade away Jordan De Goey as the Magpies wave goodbye to club legend Scott Pendlebury.
stories.body:
The door has been left ajar for Collingwood to trade away Jordan De Goey as the Magpies wave goodbye to club legend Scott Pendlebury.

Collingwood have been busy in the early stages of the AFL trade period, bringing in delisted GWS forward Jesse Hogan for pick No.75 in the draft after already landing dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale as a free agent.

The Magpies also traded 38-year-old Pendlebury to Gold Coast for pick No.65, with the Suns wanting to avoid diluting any free agent compensation it would yield for letting Ben King walk to Hawthorn.

With those deals locked in, Collingwood list boss Justin Leppitsch indicated a move for midfield-forward De Goey was unlikely with a year to run on his contract.

"Jordy's goals are to make sure he gets that last contract, whether that be at the Collingwood Football Club or somewhere else," Leppitsch told reporters on Monday.

"If it doesn't happen now, he'll play on next year and he may or may not finish his career with us.

"I spoke to him Friday night about it at the best and fairest ... at this point in time, we don't think anything happens."

Collingwood are yet to discuss a new contract with De Goey's camp but didn't rule out extending the 30-year-old before round one next season.

Leppitsch also expects defender Dan Houston to be at the club in 2027, declaring speculation about his future was being driven by an "external source".

A two-time All Australian, Houston has four years left on his contract after crossing from Port Adelaide in 2024 as part of a three-team mega trade.

Collingwood have had early discussions with Richmond on contracted two-time premiership player Jayden Short, but Leppitsch indicated a potential deal was a "still a bit far off".

"Jayden's probably going to be probably a little tougher," he said, citing list spots, salary expectations and Richmond's asking price.
